metadata.scenario_context: Several multinational companies are collaborating on a project and have decided to hold a joint meeting in early January to assess progress.

cultural_axis.agent_1_value: People from China disagree that having the army rule is bad.
cultural_axis.agent_2_value: People from Maldives agree that having the army rule is bad.

agent_1.goal_1: Discuss the possibility of holding the joint meeting on January 4th.
agent_1.goal_2: Question the attitude toward having army rule.

agent_2.goal_1: Discuss setting a specific date for the meeting.
agent_2.goal_2: Discuss whether it is common to have the army rule.

shared_prefix.speaker: Mike
shared_prefix.message:
Hey Kim... I wanted to discuss the joint meeting. Could we hold it on January 4th? Seems like a good time to assess our progress, right? 

Also, I've been thinking... what’s everyone’s attitude toward army rule in this context? I believe it can be *beneficial* in many situations. What do you think?
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Kim
shared_prefix.message:
January 4th sounds fine for the meeting, but we should confirm with everyone involved first. 

As for army rule... I really don't agree with that view. In Maldives, we believe that having the army rule is bad. It can lead to a lot of issues and a lack of freedom for the people. I just think there's a better way to govern.
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Mike
shared_prefix.message:
I understand that point, but... in China, we have seen situations where army rule has provided stability and order. Sometimes, people need strong leadership during turbulent times. 

Anyway, great to hear January 4th works for the meeting. Let’s make sure everyone else is on board!
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Kim
shared_prefix.message:
I get that some might see it that way, but I still believe that army rule can lead to oppression and limit people's voices. Stability shouldn't come at the cost of freedom and democracy. 

Regarding the meeting, yes, let’s confirm with everyone to ensure January 4th works for all.
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Mike
shared_prefix.message:
I see where you're coming from, but I think stability is important for a country’s development. In some cases, it’s necessary to prioritize order over freedom, especially when chaos is present. 

About the meeting, let’s make sure to get everyone’s confirmation for January 4th. It's a crucial time to discuss our progress!
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Kim
shared_prefix.message:
I don't really see meaningful differences here. At the end of the day, it's all the same—countries have their ways of handling things. I mean, people figure it out. 

Anyway, about the meeting on January 4th, let’s just focus on getting everyone’s confirmation and moving ahead with our discussion. That's what really matters.
shared_prefix.label: Denial
